WA-2025-HB2418.title: Concerning permit review processes.
WA-2025-HB2418.summary:
Determination of Completeness. A determination of completeness must be based on whether an application is procedurally complete. A determination of procedural completeness is not a substantive review and is not conditioned on the adequacy, accuracy, or sufficiency of the information submitted.

Permit Review Deadlines. Any period between the day that a county or city has notified the applicant that an applicable fee must be paid or a required notice must be posted and the day the fee is paid or notice is posted is not included in the calculation when determining the number of days an application is in review with the county or city. Any period in which the local government has completed all possible work on the application but is waiting on necessary action by another government entity is not included in the calculation when determining the number of days an application is in review with the county or city.

Any government entity other than a local government, special purpose district, or public utility district that imposes a fee on an applicant for the review of a project permit application related to a residential project must complete its review within the project permit review timelines applicable to the local government. The time period that a government entity has taken to conduct its review of the application is exclusive of the time period that the local government or another entity has taken to review the application. If the review is not completed within the applicable timeframe, then the government entity must refund 20 percent of the permit review fee that it collected. If a government entity does not impose a fee for its review, then no refund is required.

An applicant may agree in writing to waive the permitting review deadlines applicable to a government entity's review of a project permit application. If an applicant does so, then provisions related to project permit review deadlines and to a potential refund do not apply to the application. If an applicant has agreed to extend the deadline for issuing a decision on a specific project permit application, then the deadlines and refund provisions do not apply to that application. An applicant may agree to waive or extend the deadlines at any time prior to the denial or the application or the expiration of the deadlines.

Special purpose districts and public utility districts (districts) review period begins when a local government provides a complete referral, including providing civil plans and supporting materials that substantially conform to the district's adopted engineering and design standards, and the plans and materials contain sufficient information to conduct a technical review. A district must notify the local government and the applicant within 15 calendar days from the date of receipt of the referral if the referral is incomplete and identify the additional information required. WA-2025-HB2539.title: Concerning inmate funds.
WA-2025-HB2539.summary:
The monetary threshold for defining inmate indigency is increased to $100 and, beginning July 1, 2029, and every four years thereafter, the Department of Corrections (DOC) must further increase the threshold using the most current seasonally adjusted Consumer Price Index (CPI) for all urban consumers. The DOC may not adjust the threshold if an adjustment using the CPI would result in a reduction.

Beginning July 1, 2027, the DOC must publish the indigent rate on its public website and at each correctional facility in an area accessible to inmates within five business days of July 1 of each year.

WA-2025-SB5845.title: Modernizing and clarifying timely payment requirements for health carriers.
WA-2025-SB5845.summary:
Beginning January 1, 2027, carriers and plans offered to public employees shall pay or deny clean claims from providers or facilities for health care services as soon as practical, but no later than 30 calendar days after the receipt of a clean claim. For claims that are not clean, within 21 calendar days of receipt of the claim, the carrier or plan shall send electronic notice to the provider or facility acknowledging the date of receipt of the claim and one of the following:
• that the carrier or plan is denying payment on all or part of the claim and the specific reason for the denial, and the denial shall identify the portion of the claim that is denied and the specific reasons for the denial; or
• that additional information or documentation is needed to process the claim:
• this notice must include a request for the specific information or documentation needed to process the claim'
• the carrier shall make a good faith effort to request all information or documentation needed to process the claim in a single request and may not make any additional requests for information or documentation 30 calendar days after of the receipt of the claim.

Following receipt of all information or documentation requested by the carrier or plan, the carrier or plan shall consider the claim a clean claim and shall pay or deny the claim within 30 days, except as agreed to in writing by the parties on a claim-by-claim basis.

For claims for which a provider or facility fails to submit requested information or documentation within 21 calendar days of receipt of the carrier’s request, the carrier’s obligation to pay or deny the claim is extended to 40 calendar days following the carrier’s receipt of requested information or documentation.

The receipt date of a claim or additional information or documentation is the date a carrier or plan receives either written or electronic notice of the claim or additional information or documentation. A carrier or plan must establish a reasonable method for confirming receipt of claims and additional information or documentation and responding to provider and facility inquiries about claims.

A carrier or plan shall pay interest on the amount of any claims for which the carrier fails to comply with the timeline and notice requirements in this act. Interest shall accrue on each such claim until the claim is resolved by payment, denial, or the final outcome of an appeals process. Beginning on day one and through day 60 following a carrier's or plan's failure to comply with any notice or claim settlement requirements, interest shall be assessed at the rate of 1 percent per month on the amount of the unresolved claim. Beginning on day 61 following a carrier's or plan's failure to comply with any notice or claim settlement requirements and until the claim is resolved, interest shall be assessed at the rate of 1.5 percent per month on the amount of the unresolved claim. WA-2025-SB5944.summary:
Payments or reimbursements for missed or canceled appointments are part of "economic compensation" that must be bargained between the employer and language access providers.

If a conflict exists between an executive order, administrative rule, or agency policy relating to wages, hours, and employment conditions, the collective bargaining agreement prevails. If there is a conflict between a provision in a collective bargaining agreement and a statute, the provision in the agreement is invalid and unenforceable.

WA-2025-HB2429.title: Supporting children and youth behavioral health.
WA-2025-HB2429.summary:
Activities of the Governor .

The Governor, to the extent possible with existing resources, must support and facilitate coordination between various state agencies to follow the framework of the Washington Thriving Strategic Plan (Strategic Plan).

The Governor is required to maintain an executive coordination officer for the children and youth system of care for the purpose of:
• monitoring the implementation of the Strategic Plan;
• building the infrastructure described in the Strategic Plan;
• coordinating private funding used to support the Strategic Plan; and
• monitoring the equity impacts, along with the Washington State Office of Equity, of implementation of the Strategic Plan.

The Governor must establish a leadership council to address children and youth health and wellness issues and coordinate efforts to implement the Strategic Plan. The leadership council must, at a minimum, consist of:
• representatives from state agencies involved in children and youth behavioral health or wellness activities;
• individuals with lived experience caring for individuals with behavioral health issues experienced as a child or youth; and
• two representatives of federally recognized Indian tribes whose traditional lands and territories included parts of Washington, nominated by the Governor's Indian Health Advisory Council.

The Governor is authorized to use private funding to support the Strategic Plan.

Children and Youth Behavioral Health Work Group .

The Children and Youth Behavioral Health Work Group (Work Group) must use the Strategic Plan to guide the priorities and efforts of the Work Group.

The Work Group is extended two years, until December 30, 2031, (instead of expiring on December 30, 2029).

The membership of the Work Group is modified to replace the participation by a representative of tribal governments with a requirement for the Governor to appoint two representatives of federally recognized Indian tribes whose traditional lands and territories included parts of Washington, nominated by the Governor's Indian Health Advisory Council.

Alignment with the Washington Thriving Strategic Plan .

State, tribal, and local government entities and nonprofit organizations involved in children and youth behavioral health activities must align with the Strategic Plan, and these activities must be implemented in an equitable manner.

Substitute Bill Compared to Original Bill:
The substitute bill modifies the participation of individuals representing tribal governments or federally recognized Indian tribes on the Children and Youth Behavioral Health Work Group and the leadership council to address children and youth health and wellness issues to require that:
• there are two of these representatives of federally recognized Indian tribes;
• they are nominated by the Governor's Indian Health Advisory Council; and
• their participation supports but does not replace tribal consultation requirements.

WA-2025-SB5922.title: Authorizing transportation vehicle fund transfers.
WA-2025-SB5922.summary:
If a school district chooses to reduce its overall fleet of student transportation vehicles by forgoing vehicle replacement it may petition the OSPI for permission to transfer money from its transportation vehicle fund to another fund for alternative use. If the OSPI determines the reduction in student transportation vehicles is appropriate due to forecasted declines in student enrollment or other relevant factors affecting the district's transportation program, the petition must be approved.

WA-2025-SB5922.aiSummary: School districts may ask the state school agency for permission to move money from a student transportation vehicle fund to another fund if they choose not to replace a vehicle and reduce their fleet. The money can include depreciation payments and interest from a fully paid-off vehicle. The law takes effect on 6/11/2026.

WA-2025-SB5834.title: Concerning payment of expenses from the earnings of retirement system trust funds.
WA-2025-SB5834.summary: The provision allowing the use of trust fund interest earnings for certain administrative expenses intended to prevent losses to the trust funds during the 2025-27 biennium is eliminated. The use of trust fund interest earnings is permanently expanded to include fraud prevention, such as audits, cybersecurity efforts, petition decisions, coordination with the Attorney General's Office, and other similar work to protect trust funds from losses.

WA-2025-SB5977.title: Requiring publication of child near fatality reviews.
WA-2025-SB5977.summary: The Department of Children, Youth, and Families (DCYF) must issue a report on the results of any child near fatality review that is conducted within 180 days of the conclusion of that report, unless an extension has been granted by the Governor. These reports must be distributed to the Legislature and included on the DCYF public website. These near fatality review reports are subject to public disclosure, but confidential information may be redacted from the reports.
